messages:
raj: Canary started failing on dedicated-gpu-us-east-2 at ~03:10 UTC, several OOMs in the same autoscaler group. Node IDs: gw-3, gw-7.

emily: saw a deploy around 03:05? link: https://ci.redwood/changes/4821 :thinking_face:

deploy-bot: change 4821 merged by emily at 03:04:58 UTC (batching: adaptive-boundary heuristic).

raj: stack traces show kv_slab_alloc -> kv_grow_slab -> kernel_select_fallback during alloc hotpath. OOM logs attached (snippet):
```
[OOM] pid=3214 vm=1.8G slab_alloc failed size=131072 path=kv_slab_alloc
backtrace:
  0x7f6c2 kv_slab_alloc+0x3f
  0x7f7a kv_prefetch_alloc+0x1b
  0x5b9c batch_dispatcher_handle+0x2a
```

liam: also seeing memory climb on longseq workloads (avg seqlen 2048). curious if adaptive-boundary changes batch boundaries and increases in-flight KV cache retention.

sophia: can we reproduce with the canary job? raj, can you dump /proc/<pid>/smaps on gw-3 when it spikes?

raj: running reproducer now. command: `./tools/run_canary --profile=longseq --concurrency=12 --kernel=auto --batch-heuristic=adaptive`

infra-bot: perf test `canary-longseq-420987` triggered: 4/5 instances OOM within 90s. Auto-pinned to release-2026-03-18-4821.

emily: note that PR 4821 changed batching boundary logic + introduced a kernel-selection tie-break where we prefer cudnn-like kernels for small batches. Might interact with our KV cache warmup.

liam: hypothesis: adaptive-boundary merges more requests into fewer batches; long sequences cause larger KV cache footprints per batch, plus a kernel fallback path that allocates a transient buffer ~128KB per request. With higher concurrency this multiplies into OOMs.

sophia: if that's true, a quick revert of the adaptive-boundary flag should calm canaries. Can we toggle the feature flag in config to disable without full revert?

emily: I can flip the rollout flag for canaries. Rolling back global merge is heavier. Reverting flag for canary pools now.

deploy-bot: rollout update: adaptive-boundary=false for cluster dedicated-gpu-us-east-2 (canaries only). Change applied at 03:26 UTC.

raj: after toggle, new canary started, memory looks stable for 10m. no OOMs in latest run.

perf-bot: CI perf check failed: `kv-memory-stability` regression +12% memory compared to baseline on job longseq-4x. Failure triggered at 03:18 UTC on CI runs that include change 4821.

liam: OK that's consistent. Next steps: 1) produce minimal repro that exercises kernel fallback + batch coalescing, 2) bisect micro-change in PR 4821 (there are 4 commits), 3) add an alloc accounting gauge in runtime to see per-batch transient allocations.

emily: I'm bisecting locally across the 4 commits now. If anyone finds a quick in-proc patch to avoid fallback allocations, post it here.

raj: attaching a heap-profile from gw-3 when it spikes (uploaded to /mnt/artifacts/420987/gw-3.heap). Summary: high number of small transient allocations (~64-256B) plus a chunk of 128KB buffers showing up in tcmalloc arenas.

liam: interesting — fragmentation amplifies with many small allocs; combined with large transient 128KB (likely kernel temp buffer) means slabs become unusable and we hit reserve. Can we try forcing kernel selection to the old codepath on canary: `--kernel=legacy-select`?

emily: tried legacy-select locally with the reproducer, memory stays within expected envelope. That's a strong signal the new tie-breaker path is culprit.

sophia: let's open an emergency revert of the kernel tie-break commit and keep adaptive-boundary disabled for canaries until revert lands. I'll file the revert PR and flag it as rollout-blocker.

emily: PR 4836 created: "revert: kernel-selection tie-break (temp revert)". Setting for expedited review.

raj: re-run canary with PR 4836 applied + adaptive-boundary=false. No OOMs in 30m stress run.

liam: follow-ups: - add unit that simulates high fragmentation and asserts reserve never drops below threshold; - add metric that exposes per-batch transient-alloc bytes; - consider moving the 128KB buffer into an arena friendly pool to avoid eviction pressure.

sophia: agreed. Also add test case in qemu CI for longseq+high-concurrency to catch regressions earlier.

emily: thanks all — keeping the canary off adaptive-boundary and reverting kernel tie-break. Will shepherd perf regression ticket and ensure we don't merge any kernel selection changes without memory footprint validation. :thumbsup:
